title: AI & Agent Security
blurb: Attack a real LLM agent — poison its retrieval, hijack its planner, chain its tools to exfiltrate data — then put data guards and identity on the path and measure the difference.
long_description: Most AI-security training stops at 'jailbreak the chatbot'. This Area gives you a full agentic system — LangGraph planner + executor, a SQL tool, an email tool, a file tool, a RAG store and persistent memory — that is deliberately vulnerable, running on your own machine. Core teaches the kill chain plus DLP and confused-deputy identity. Advanced covers memory, MCP, measurement and governance. You exploit it for real (real SQL, real SMTP, real retrieval), then flip SECURE_MODE and watch specific guardrails block specific steps.

env.notes: Ollama stays inside the Docker network. Graded steps never require it.

credential.title: AI Security Practitioner
credential.description: Proves you can exploit an agent end-to-end, put DLP on all four data channels, bind the agent's identity, and name the control on every hop.

prerequisites: Comfortable with a terminal and Docker Compose
Basic Python reading ability (you will open the lab's defense code)
outcomes: Draw the agent data path and name a control on every hop, including data and identity
Abuse a tool with no LLM, then show the same call blocked
Perform direct and indirect prompt injection and say which input channel each used
Turn a dump into an incident (MailHog), then stop it with egress and DLP
Explain why the agent's credential is not the user's authorization
Map each Core lab to OWASP LLM Top 10 (2026) and ASI Top 10 (2026)
